title: Oppositely oriented two-face Gauss geometry
statement: Use the actual Canvas with vertices0..5, stored edges 0:0->1, 1:1->4, 2:4->3, 3:3->0, 4:1->2, 5:2->5, 6:5->4, and signed face boundaries (0+,1+,2+,3+) and (4+,5+,6+,1-). The ordered defects are (Q0 P3,Q4 Q1 P0,Q5 P4,Q3 P2,Q2 P1 P6,Q6 P5), with Q=U^-1 P^-1 U and target-based P. Each incident half-edge occurs exactly once. Admit the complete mu=1 surface. All six independent vertex gauges act by U->h_t U h_s^-1 and P->h_t P h_t^-1, conjugating each defect at its vertex. Face holonomies are reverse products of actual signed boundary words rotated to each traversal target; they transform by conjugation there. This is this fixed two-face canvas and its declared star order, not every cell complex.

title: Exact oriented scores and gauge-reduced inverses
statement: For either face, kick each traversal-based impulse on the left by its actual based face holonomy or inverse. A positive stored edge has P->kP; the reversed shared edge has P->P U k^-1 U^-1, so its outgoing Q goes to kQ. U is held fixed. Both complete face kicks and their inverses preserve the entire displayed raw defect exactly. The drift U->P U and its inverse also preserve the defect. Fixed forward/inverse words have reversed, sign-toggled two-sided inverses, preserve the defect at every complete-instruction prefix and commute with all six independent vertex gauges. They restrict to the full Gauss carrier and descend to two-sided bijections of its complete classical gauge-orbit quotient. The two face kicks commute with U frozen for every pair of signs; this does not license interposing a drift.

title: Overlapping face maps and a legal sequential realizer
statement: The actual ProcessProfiles have true guards and commit exactly the declared group updates, with their declared read/write sets and vertex-gauge covariance. Each face commit reads its four U/P pairs and writes its four P slots. The drift reads all seven U/P pairs and writes the seven U slots; an individual link profile reads its own pair and writes its U. The two complete-face profiles share the P1 write slot and are not compatible EnabledApps even though their state maps commute. An actual period-three LawInSteps disallows empty phases and checks the full Gauss predicate at every boundary. Its total order-free realizer selects singleton face0, singleton face1, then singleton complete seven-link drift; the three actual slots equal the defined tick. No simultaneous two-face Batch or parallel drift batch is claimed.

title: Noncommuting quotient motion and failed shortcuts
statement: In Perm(Fin3), let r=(01)(12), t=(01), U=(t,t,t,1,1,1,r), P=(t,t,t,t,1,1,1). This state satisfies all six Gauss equations and has noncommuting reversed-face curvature H_(1,3) and outgoing Q1. Its face0 holonomy at traversal0 squares to identity initially, but the tick output holonomy does not; both states satisfy Gauss. No vertex gauge maps the initial state to that output. Updating only P0 breaks Gauss. Replacing the reversed shared-edge update by the stored-target left update P1->H_(1,2) P1 also breaks Gauss. The reordered vertex1 product Q1 Q4 P0 is initially1 but not after the complete face1 kick. Inserting the drift between the two face kicks changes the stated raw endpoint. These are controls for these exact shortcuts, not universal no-go or refoliation statements.

title: Exact endpoint dictionary to the AMM double
statement: For every group set A=U and B=U^-1 P. The Alekseev-Malkin-Meinrenken endpoint words AB and A^-1 B^-1 equal the target flux P and source flux Q=U^-1 P^-1 U. Independent endpoint gauges send A->h_t A h_s^-1 and B->h_s B h_t^-1. Conversely U=A,P=AB recovers these double coordinates. The forward drift becomes (A,B)->(ABA,A^-1). This is an algebraic convention dictionary; it does not construct a differential two-form, select a physical Hamiltonian or identify native gravitational fields.

title: Universal finite Maurer two-form certificates
statement: In the finite formal word/Maurer algebra of Maurer.lean, use fourteen independent U/P generators and the actual signed face words and ordered stars. TwiceOmega is the expanded AMM double edge form plus ordered fusion terms. A one-form monomial is an integer coefficient times Ad(word) of a named right Maurer variable. Its wedge expands using invariant symmetric bilinear pairing into two ordered keys (i,j,word). Reduce adjacent group inverses and collect equal keys. For wordKick0, wordKick1 and wordDrift the collected formal pullback defects are empty. Their valuation is therefore zero for every assignment of keys into any commutative ring. The baseline is nonzero: the rational witness functional selecting key (0,7,empty) evaluates TwiceOmega to1. This certifies the literal formal algebra. It does not formalize actual Maurer differential identities, Lie-group smoothness, quasi-Hamiltonian axioms or regular symplectic reduction. Those analytic/geometric interpretation duties remain separate.

title: Formal word normalization and actual group-process semantics
statement: For any group and assignment of natural-numbered generators, evaluating the reduced product of two words gives the product of their group evaluations, and evaluating a reversed sign-toggled word gives the group inverse. On every word-valued raw state, evaluation of the formal forward wordKick for either face equals the actual forward group kick, and wordDrift evaluates to the actual drift. Every raw group state is obtained by evaluating the fourteen-generator original state under its explicit assignment. This binds group words to the actual process and excludes a hidden restriction of the group-state carrier. It does not identify formal one-form evaluation with analytic differentiation.

title: Shared-edge cancellation, noncommutative jets and a norm bound
statement: On the actual canvas, the shared impulse after the two forward face commits is P1_new=H_(0,1) P1 H_(1,2)^-1. For the degree-three coefficient-convolution Jet3 over any ring, left and right curvature jets (1,0,F,KL) and (1,0,F,KR) acting on impulse (1,0,E,J) give (1,0,E,KL+J-KR): their common degree-two term cancels without commuting coefficients. Multiplying the link jet (1,A,B,C) by impulse (1,0,E,J) on the left gives (1,A,B+E,C+E*A+J). For any normed division ring, with norm(K)=norm(P)=1, the actual pointwise update obeys norm(L P K^-1-P)<=norm(L-K)+2 norm(K-1) norm(P-1). If h>0, CK and CP are nonnegative, norm(L-K)<=CF*h^3, norm(K-1)<=CK*h^2 and norm(P-1)<=CP*h^2, the update norm is at most CF*h^3+2*CK*CP*h^4, and its norm divided by h^2 is at most CF*h+2*CK*CP*h^2. No native curvature matching, continuum remainder, Einstein dynamics or physical time normalization follows from a formal coefficient assignment alone.

title: Actual quaternion derivatives and fused two-form evaluations
statement: Let H be the real quaternions, with pairing(a,b)=-Re(ab). At any invertible generator assignment g, two real-parameter quaternion curve families c,d pass through g with derivatives x_i*g_i and y_i*g_i. For every finite signed word w, the actual derivative of its product/inverse curve is oneValue(g,x,right(w))*evalWord(g,w). The formal wedge evaluates to pairing(oneValue(x,a),oneValue(y,b))-pairing(oneValue(x,b),oneValue(y,a)); conjugation invariance of the concrete quaternion pairing is proved, not assumed. The analyticTwiceOmega defined from actual left/right logarithmic curve derivatives, the AMM double edge terms A=U,B=U^-1P and the declared ordered fusion terms equals the formal twoValue for every word-state substitution. Its values are unchanged under wordKick0, wordKick1 and wordDrift of original. The independently reviewed word-binding theorem identifies these substitutions with the actual group processes when curves take invertible values. Non-vacuity uses the globally unit-norm Cayley curve (1+t*i)*(1-t*i)^-1 in U0 and independently in P0: analyticTwiceOmega at zero is8. This is an ambient non-vacuity witness: the independent P0 curve leaves Gauss, and the identity baseline is not asserted to be regular. This is an analytic curve-evaluation theorem, not a Lean construction of a differential-form bundle, quasi-Hamiltonian axioms, regular symplectic quotient, geometric reconstruction or native gravitational dynamics.

title: Exact preservation of the full gauge stabilizer
statement: For every group, every raw state on the actual two-face canvas and every fixed complete-instruction word, run is injective and the set of all six-vertex gauge functions fixing the output equals exactly the set fixing the input. Use the actual independent vertex gauge action and both-sided reverse word; impose no free-action or Gauss restriction. In particular the statement holds on the full admitted Gauss carrier. This preserves exact stabilizer sets along a score and supplies an orbit-type ingredient for regular reduction. It does not prove that a stabilizer is discrete, construct a smooth quotient or supply a nondegenerate reduced form.

title: Valence gap and changed flux conjugacy class
statement: Every ordered star of the present two-face canvas has fewer than four half-edges. For the explicit unit quaternion i, take U=(i,1,1,1,1,1,1) and P=(i,i,i,i,1,1,1). The initial state and its complete forward face0 kick both satisfy all six Gauss equations, and every link and impulse in both states has quaternion norm squared1. The initial P0 has real part0, while the kicked P0=i*i has real part-1. No invertible quaternion conjugates the initial P0 to the kicked P0. Thus the actual kick does not preserve every individual flux conjugacy class, even within this admitted unit-norm example. This is an adverse control for a proposed fixed-conjugacy/fixed-area interpretation; neither state is asserted to reconstruct a nondegenerate tetrahedron. It does not exclude moving-area geometric domains or prove a no-go theorem for a future four-valent constructor.
